recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if a later final tracker changes VisionPrescription's official category or explicitly requires removal of financial-module contextual links; the current source satisfies FHIR-7425.
issue_request: FHIR-7425 was a Published / Persuasive FHIR-core DSTU1 change request asking that VisionPrescription be treated as a clinical resource, like other prescriptions or orders, rather than as non-clinical or merely financial content. The Jira resolution says this was already in STU3.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-7425 was found in the bounded history search. The Jira disposition records the change as already applied by STU3. Later source history introduced explicit resource-category tooling in commit 687407e2959b695e71aeea5a80596c5b225b36da with VisionPrescription in Clinical.Care Provision, and subsequent refactors carried that category into the current StructureDefinition metadata and resource list.
additional_context: FHIR-5639 is a same-family Published tracker asking for VisionPrescription to be under Orders and describing it as a clinical order rather than financial content. Current workflow and clinical-summary pages list VisionPrescription with clinical orders/resources. Later FHIR-39279 retained VisionPrescription and moved custodianship to Orders and Observations; that issue is already represented on the combined branch by commit 389cab6493dfada990d24e42675e8c1b1da10b20. The financial module still cross-links VisionPrescription for reimbursement and authorization context, but that contextual navigation does not override the authoritative Clinical.Care Provision category.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current source already has VisionPrescription active in source/fhir.ini, assigns it to OO, sets structuredefinition-category to Clinical.Care Provision, maps it to Clinical.Care Provision in publish.ini, places it under Clinical.Care Provision in source/resourcelist.html, and presents it in workflow as an order.

related_jiras.note: Earlier Published/Persuasive request to put VisionPrescription under Orders reinforces the same clinical-order classification.
Later Published decision retained VisionPrescription and moved ownership/custodianship to OO; it is already audited on the combined branch.
Resolved No Change request about replacing VisionPrescription with a generic authorization resource records that the separate resource was intentionally retained.
